q: 1. Who are the members of Council of Ministers of SAARC?
options: Ministers of foreign affairs of the members state
Ministers of prime ministers of the members state
Ministers of defence ministers of the members state
Ministers of home ministers of the members state
explain: The SAARC Council of Ministers comprises the Foreign Ministers of member states and meets to formulate policy.

q: 2. Who is the Nepali artist to design the SAARC emblem?
explain: The SAARC emblem was designed by Nepali artist Shailendra Kumar Mahrajan.

q: 3. When was the 18th Summit of SAARC in Kathmandu held?
explain: The 18th SAARC Summit was held in Kathmandu, Nepal from 26-27 November 2014.

q: 4. When did SAARC Convention on preventing and combating Trafficking in women and children for prostitution signed in Kathmandu?
explain: The SAARC Convention on Preventing and Combating Trafficking in Women and Children for Prostitution was signed at the 11th SAARC Summit held in Kathmandu in 2002.

q: 5. When was SAFTA (South Asian Free Trade Agreement) signed during 12th Summit in Islamabad on?
explain: SAFTA was signed on 6 January 2004 at the 12th SAARC Summit in Islamabad.

q: 6. When was SAARC framework agreement for energy Co-operation signed on?
explain: The SAARC Framework Agreement on Energy Cooperation was signed on 27 November 2014 during the 18th Summit in Kathmandu.

q: 7. Afghanistan participated as the 8th member of SAARC?
explain: Afghanistan formally joined SAARC as its eighth member during the 14th SAARC Summit held in New Delhi in 2007.

q: 8. Which SAARC summit envisioned the established of South Asian economic Union (SAEU)?
explain: The 18th SAARC Summit's declaration reaffirmed the long-term vision of moving towards a South Asian Economic Union (SAEU).

q: 9. When was South Asian Free Trade Area (SAFTA) come in force?
explain: Although SAFTA was signed in 2004, the agreement formally came into force on 1 January 2006.

q: 10. Where was the first summit of SAARC held in?
explain: The first SAARC Summit was held in Dhaka, Bangladesh in December 1985, where the SAARC Charter was adopted.

q: 11. Which SAARC Summit decided to establish the SAARC Development Fund (SDF) as a comprehensive funding mechanism with the provision of three windows (Social, Economic & Infrastructure)?
explain: The 13th SAARC Summit (Dhaka, 2005) decided to establish the SAARC Development Fund with Social, Economic, and Infrastructure windows.

q: 12. SAARC is observing a decade (2010-2020) of which of the following?
explain: SAARC declared 2010-2020 as the Decade of Intra-regional Connectivity to strengthen physical, economic, and people-to-people links.

q: 13. What was the theme of the SAARC year 2016-17 A.D.?
explain: SAARC observed 2016-17 as the 'Year of Cultural Heritage' to promote the region's shared cultural legacy.

q: 14. Currently, How many SAARC regional centers are in existence?
explain: SAARC originally had 11 regional centres, later consolidated and reduced to 5 to improve efficiency.

q: 15. Which SAARC Summit decided to reduce regional centre to from 11 to 5?
explain: The decision to consolidate SAARC's 11 regional centres into 5 was taken at the 18th SAARC Summit in Kathmandu (2014).

q: 16. Where is the head quarter of SAARC Chamber of commerce and industry located?
explain: The SAARC Chamber of Commerce and Industry (SCCI) has its headquarters in Islamabad, Pakistan.

q: 17. Where is SAARC cultural centre located?
explain: The SAARC Cultural Centre is located in Colombo, Sri Lanka.

q: 18. Comparing the following Regional Centers established in the SAARC nations; choose the correct answer from the code. a.Nepal b.Bangladesh c.India d.Pakistan / 1.Agricultural Centre(SAC) 2.Environment & Natural Disaster(END) 3.Energy Centre(SEC) 4.Tuberculosis Centre(STC)
explain: Nepal hosts the Tuberculosis Centre (STC), Bangladesh hosts the Agricultural Centre (SAC), India hosts the Environment & Natural Disaster centre (END), and Pakistan hosts the Energy Centre (SEC): a-4, b-1, c-2, d-3.

q: 19. Which of the following is\are not the observer of South Asian Association for Regional Co-operation (SAARC)?
explain: SAARC observers include Japan, USA, South Korea, China, EU and others, but the UK is not among SAARC's observer states.

q: 20. How many Country/Organization that granted for the observer status of South Asian Association for Regional Co-operation (SAARC)?
explain: SAARC has granted observer status to 9 countries/organizations, including Australia, China, EU, Iran, Japan, South Korea, Mauritius, Myanmar, and the USA.

q: 21. Who is Current Secretary General of South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC)?
explain: As per this reference material, Golam Sarwar is listed as the current Secretary-General of SAARC.

q: 22. Considering the area of the SAARC nations, which of the following is the right order of those Nations, from the smallest to the largest?
options: Maldives, Bhutan, Nepal, Sri Lanka, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Afghanistan, India
Bhutan, Maldives, Nepal, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh, Afghanistan, Pakistan, India
Maldives, Bhutan, Sri Lanka, Nepal, Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Pakistan, India
Maldives, Bhutan, Sri Lanka, Nepal, Bangladesh, Afghanistan, Pakistan, India
explain: By land area, the correct ascending order of SAARC nations is Maldives, Bhutan, Sri Lanka, Nepal, Bangladesh, Afghanistan, Pakistan, India.

q: 23. Which of the following SAARC country with highest population literacy rate?
explain: Maldives has the highest literacy rate among SAARC nations, close to universal literacy.

q: 24. Which is the first SAARC country to provide e-passport to its citizens?
explain: The Maldives was the first SAARC country to introduce e-passports for its citizens.

q: 25. How many land-locked countries are there in South Asian Association for Regional Co-Operation (SAARC)?
explain: SAARC has 3 land-locked countries: Nepal, Bhutan, and Afghanistan.

q: 26. How many water-locked countries are there in South Asian Association for Regional Co Operation (SAARC)?
explain: SAARC has 2 water-locked (island) countries: Sri Lanka and Maldives.

q: 27. What is the Currency of Bhutan called?
explain: Bhutan's official currency is the Ngultrum, which is pegged to the Indian Rupee.

q: 28. How many times that the SAARC summits held in Nepal?
explain: Nepal has hosted SAARC Summits three times: the 3rd (1987), 11th (2002), and 18th (2014) Summits, all held in Kathmandu.

q: 29. What percentage of total expenditure of SAARC secretariat is bear by Nepal?
explain: As per this reference, Nepal bears 10.72% of the total expenditure of the SAARC Secretariat, based on the organization's cost-sharing formula.

q: 30. When was BIMSTEC established?
explain: BIMSTEC was established on 6 June 1997 through the Bangkok Declaration.

q: 31. Which country is not the founder member of the BIMSTEC?
explain: BIMSTEC was founded in 1997 by Bangladesh, India, Sri Lanka, and Thailand; Nepal joined later, in 2004, along with Bhutan.

q: 32. BIMSTEC permanent Headquarter at Dhaka was established on --------
explain: The BIMSTEC Permanent Secretariat in Dhaka was formally established on 13 September 2014.

q: 33. Where is BIMSTEC permanent secretariat located?
explain: The BIMSTEC Permanent Secretariat is located in Dhaka, Bangladesh.

q: 34. Where was the 4th BIMSTEC summit held in 2018 A.D.?
explain: The 4th BIMSTEC Summit was held in Kathmandu, Nepal in August 2018.

q: 35. Which of the following statement is/are correct?
options: Nepal was granted the observer status of BIMSTEC in 1998
In 2018, it was expanded to embrace two more sectors including blue economy and mountain economy
Now, it has 7 areas of cooperation
explain: All three statements are correct: Nepal held observer status before becoming a full member, the sectors were expanded in 2018, and BIMSTEC now has 7 broad areas of cooperation.

q: 36. Which of the following is not the member state of BIMSTEC?
explain: BIMSTEC's seven members are Bangladesh, India, Myanmar, Sri Lanka, Thailand, Nepal, and Bhutan; Malaysia is not a member.

q: 37. When did Nepal formally get membership of BIMSTEC?
explain: Nepal formally became a member of BIMSTEC in February 2004.

q: 38. Currently, which country is the chair of BIMSTEC?
explain: As per this reference material, Bangladesh currently holds the chairmanship of BIMSTEC.

q: 39. What is the regional initiative comprising 7 member states of both SAARC and ASEAN called?
explain: BIMSTEC brings together countries bridging South Asia (SAARC) and Southeast Asia (ASEAN) around the Bay of Bengal.

q: 40. How many sectoral area of cooperation are indentified by the fifth BIMSTEC Summit held in Columbo, Sri Lanka?
explain: The 5th BIMSTEC Summit, held in Colombo, Sri Lanka, streamlined cooperation into 7 broad sectoral areas.

q: 41. Which Prime Minister of Nepal attended the 6th BIMSTEC Summit?
explain: K.P. Sharma Oli represented Nepal as Prime Minister at the 6th BIMSTEC Summit.

q: 42. 6th BIMSTEC summit was concluded in Bangkok with signing and inception of ___ points.
explain: The 6th BIMSTEC Summit in Bangkok concluded with the signing/adoption of an 18-point declaration/outcome document.

q: 43. What is the theme of 6th Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation (BIMSTEC) Summit?
options: Towards a Peaceful, Prosperous & Sustainable Bay of Bengal Region
Prosperous Economies, Healthy Peoples & Sustainable Bay of Bengal Region
explain: The 6th BIMSTEC Summit in Bangkok (2025) was held under the theme 'Prosperous, Resilient, and Open BIMSTEC'.

q: 44. At the conclusion of the 6th BIMSTEC summit, ___ took over as chair nation of BIMSTEC.
explain: Bangladesh assumed the BIMSTEC chairmanship at the conclusion of the 6th Summit in Bangkok.

q: 45. Which country was hosted the sixth BIMSTEC Summit in 2025?
explain: Thailand hosted the 6th BIMSTEC Summit in Bangkok in 2025.

q: 46. Which sector of BIMSTEC is leading by Nepal?
explain: Nepal is designated as the lead country for the People-to-People Contact sector within BIMSTEC's sectoral cooperation framework.
